topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance Toward Pi
target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Sine Power Integral
sections.content: Introduce the reduction formula for the integral of sin^n(x) from 0 to π/2. Explain that as n increases, this integral value acts as a gateway to understanding the behavior of ratios of these integrals.
sections.example: Visualize a 'folding' animation where the area under sin^n(x) shrinks and flattens against the x-axis as n grows, showing the transition from a hump to a thin spike.

sections.title: The Recursive Ratio
sections.content: Establish the relationship between I_n (the integral of sin^n(x)) and I_{n-2}. Show how the ratio I_{n}/I_{n-1} approaches 1 as n goes to infinity, leading to the construction of a product sequence.
sections.example: An animated 'scales' visual where two buckets (representing the integrals) are balanced against each other, gradually adjusting weights until they stabilize at a ratio of 1.

sections.title: Deriving the Wallis Product
sections.content: Substitute the integral results into the ratio formula. Step-by-step algebraic manipulation to isolate π/2, resulting in the elegant infinite product: π/2 = (2/1 * 2/3) * (4/3 * 4/5) * (6/5 * 6/7)...
sections.example: Display an infinite conveyor belt where number tiles (2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6...) drop into the numerator and (1, 3, 3, 5, 5, 7...) into the denominator, slowly assembling the value of π.

sections.title: Visualizing Convergence
sections.content: Demonstrate how the partial products of the Wallis formula oscillate above and below π/2, narrowing down the target value over time.
sections.example: A digital 'Target Practice' game where a character (e.g., a rabbit) jumps back and forth across the value π/2, with each jump becoming smaller until they land exactly on the center.

sections.title: Summary and Significance
sections.content: Recap the beauty of connecting pure calculus (integrals) to the fundamental circle constant (π). Emphasize that while slow to converge, it provides deep insight into the structure of numbers.
sections.example: A final visual showing the Wallis product emerging as a beautiful geometric pattern, connecting the algebraic equation to a perfect circle drawn on a coordinate plane.
